title: Cap Hestia's own requests at high; skip causes a person closed
summary: Hestia's backfill, new root-cause requests and other Hestia-queued requests (spec, throughput) are capped at high, so urgent is only for people (`athena priority`, a `Priority: urgent` line). The error review also stops re-queuing a cause whose request a person closed with `athena close`, unless a newer introspection of that cause was recorded after the close. The goal is for urgent to order the queue again, for the person running Athena.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the high cap and the person-close rule, plus fmt, clippy and test passing.
Criteria run the tests that exercise the queueing.
The cap is applied in every Hestia request builder, not only the backfill.
Doc comments and the CHANGELOG entry are updated.
One focused change, mostly in hestia.rs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs: root_cause_request (hard-codes Priority::Urgent), plan_backfill (BACKFILL_URGENT = 5 top-ranked get Urgent, the rest Normal), addressing_request (skips closed non-landed requests, so a person-closed cause is queued again), existing_request/backfill_step, error_review/try_error_review, spec_request (~line 604) and priority_for_minutes (throughput, Urgent at 10+ minutes). crates/athena-core/src/store.rs (JobState/OutcomeState derivation, line ~109 priority), crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs (athena close writes Dropped/Abandoned outcomes), crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (OutcomeState). The entry point is `athena hestia review --backfill` -> error_review_backfill -> plan_backfill. No new record or data file is added, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are unaffected. The rule is measured directly on job priority() and on the plan steps.

The request's phrase 'the requests they queue' covers all Hestia-queued requests, including spec and throughput ones, so those are capped too; the throughput scale becomes High at 5+ minutes. If the owner wants only the error review changed, the throughput and spec caps would be reverted.

A person's close is distinguished from Hestia's own requeue close (Dropped, written by Hestia) by the outcome's origin, found in manage.rs; the producer must decide how, for example by the close record's origin or note. Recurrence means an introspection of the cause (same cause_key) with a timestamp later than the close outcome.
This change does not add or tighten a refusal rule on readings, so no newly-refused-readings percentage applies; it only holds back Hestia from queueing.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs shows that plan_backfill over records with more than five repeated causes queues every request at Priority::High or lower (none urgent), and that root_cause_request produces a `Priority: high` request, not urgent. Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`.

A test shows a cause whose earlier request was closed with `athena close` (the manage.rs close path) gets no new request or requeue from the backfill or the per-job error review. A second case shows it is queued again, at high, once a new introspection of that cause is recorded after the close. Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`.

The backfill and the error review still queue a cause whose request was closed by Hestia itself (requeue Dropped) or was rejected or failed. A test covers at least one of these. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

BACKFILL_URGENT and the Priority::Urgent uses in Hestia's request builders (root-cause, spec_request, throughput priority_for_minutes) are removed or capped at High. Grep shows no Priority::Urgent in non-test code of hestia.rs. `athena priority` and a person-written `Priority: urgent` line are unchanged: the plan.rs/store.rs parsing of urgent is untouched.
Doc comments in hestia.rs (module docs, plan_backfill, root_cause_request) and any docs mention of urgent for Hestia are updated to say high at most.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that names the cap at high and the no-requeue after a person's close.

out_of_scope: Changing `athena priority`, plan.rs priority parsing, or letting people mark requests urgent
Re-prioritising items already in the queue, including 7ym7 and gdgv
Changing the repeat threshold or the ranking of causes
departures: A little costlier and slightly less likely to pass than the reference: hestia.rs is large, many existing tests assert Urgent and need updating, and telling a person's close from Hestia's own close needs care.
